name: Adult Autism Spectrum Quotient (AQ)
description: A 50-item self-administered instrument for measuring the degree to which an adult with normal intelligence has the traits associated with the autistic spectrum. The 50 questions are made up of 10 questions assessing five different areas: - social skill (items 1, 11, 13, 15, 22, 36, 44, 45, 47, 48); - attention switching (items 2, 4, 10, 16, 25, 32, 34, 37, 43, 46); - attention to detail (items 5, 6, 9, 12, 19, 23, 28, 29, 30, 49); - communication (items 7, 17, 18, 26, 27, 31, 33, 35, 38, 39); -
citation: Cohen S, Wheelwright S, Skinner R, Martin J, Clubley E (2001). The autism-spectrum quotient (AQ): evidence from Asperger syndrome/high-functioning autism, males and females, scientists and mathematicians. *J Autism Dev Disord.* 31(1): 5-17. Erratum in: *J Autism Dev Disord.* 2001 Dec;31(6):603. https://doi.org/10.1023/a:1005653411471 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11439754/

name: Artificial Intelligence Anxiety Scale
description: 21-item measure of anxiety toward artificial intelligence (Wang & Wang), with four factors: Learning (8 items), Job Replacement (6 items), Sociotechnical Blindness (4 items), and AI Configuration (3 items). Items are rated 1-7; subscales are averaged and the total is summed (21-147), with higher scores indicating greater AI anxiety. Includes the original English and a validated German translation.
citation: Wang, Y.-Y., & Wang, Y.-S. (2022). Development and validation of an artificial intelligence anxiety scale: An initial application in predicting motivated learning behavior. Interactive Learning Environments, 30(4), 619-634. https://doi.org/10.1080/10494820.2019.1674887

name: Big Five Inventory-2
description: A 44-item measure of the Big Five personality traits (Extraversion, Agreeableness, Conscientiousness, Neuroticism, Openness) using short trait-descriptive phrases. Items use a 5-point scale (1=disagree strongly to 5=agree strongly). Several items are reverse-scored. Widely used in personality research across cultures. Originally developed in English; Swahili translation from Garrashi et al. (2023).
citation: John, O. P., Donahue, E. M., & Kentle, R. L. (1991). The Big Five Inventory—Versions 4a and 54. University of California, Berkeley, Institute of Personality and Social Research.
license: Non-commercial research use; freely available from Berkeley Personality Lab

name: Big Five Inventory-Short
description: 15-item short measure of the Big Five personality traits (3 items per trait). Scored as mean per dimension on a 1-7 scale.
citation: Lang, F. R., John, D., Ludtke, O., Schupp, J., & Wagner, G. G. (2011). Short assessment of the Big Five: Robust across survey methods except telephone interviewing. Behavior Research Methods, 43(2), 548-567. https://doi.org/10.3758/s13428-011-0066-z

name: English Translation of the SJT-TW (Situational Judgment Test – Teamwork)
description: 12-scenario Situational Judgment Test assessing knowledge about teamwork effectiveness. Each scenario describes a work-situation faced by a team or team member and presents four behavioural response options; the respondent selects the single best (most suitable) option. The original German version (Gatzka & Volmer, 2017) additionally asks for the worst option; this English translation pilot asked only for the best option to reduce duration. Scoring against a predefined best/worst key (restricted; available from the authors). Authors propose a single total score; a tentative two-factor structure was reported but the authors recommend computing only a total test score.
citation: Freudenstein, J.-P., Remmert, N., Reznik, N., & Krumm, S. (2020). English Translation of the SJT-TW. Zusammenstellung sozialwissenschaftlicher Items und Skalen (ZIS). https://doi.org/10.6102/zis285

name: Flourishing Scale
description: 8-item summary measure of psychological well-being covering social relationships, meaning, purpose, and self-esteem.
citation:
Diener, E., Wirtz, D., Tov, W., Kim-Prieto, C., Choi, D., Oishi, S., & Biswas-Diener, R. (2010). New well-being measures: Short scales to assess flourishing and positive and negative feelings. Social Indicators Research, 97(2), 143–156. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11205-009-9493-y

Arabic translation: AL-Dossary, S. A. (2021). Psychometric properties and measurement invariance of the Arabic version of the Flourishing Scale. International Journal of Psychological Studies, 13(2), 20–27. https://doi.org/10.5539/ijps.v13n2p20

name: General Life Satisfaction Short Scale (L-1)
description: Single-item ultra-short scale measuring general (global) life satisfaction. The respondent rates overall satisfaction with their life on an 11-point rating scale (0-10). The scale score equals the respondent's answer to the one item. English-language adaptation (validated in the United Kingdom) of the German source instrument by Beierlein, Kovaleva, Laszlo, et al. (2015).
citation: Nießen, D., Groskurth, K., Rammstedt, B., & Lechner, C. M. (2021). General Life Satisfaction Short Scale (L-1). Zusammenstellung sozialwissenschaftlicher Items und Skalen (ZIS). https://doi.org/10.6102/zis284

name: General Self-Efficacy Short Scale-3 (GSE-3)
description: 3-item English-language adaptation of the German ASKU (Allgemeine Selbstwirksamkeit Kurzskala) measuring general self-efficacy: the generalized belief in one's competence to cope with a broad range of demanding or novel situations. All three items are positively keyed (no reverse items) and load on a single dimension. Answered on a fully labelled 5-point apply scale; the score is the unweighted mean of the three items.
citation: Doll, E. S., Nießen, D., Schmidt, I., Rammstedt, B., & Lechner, C. M. (2021). General Self-Efficacy Short Scale-3 (GSE-3). Zusammenstellung sozialwissenschaftlicher Items und Skalen (ZIS). https://doi.org/10.6102/zis294

name: Gratitude Questionnaire-6
description: 6-item scale measuring dispositional gratitude — the tendency to notice and appreciate the positive in life. One of the most widely used gratitude measures.
citation: McCullough, M. E., Emmons, R. A., & Tsang, J. A. (2002). The grateful disposition: A conceptual and empirical topography. Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 82(1), 112–127. https://doi.org/10.1037/0022-3514.82.1.112

name: Highly Sensitive Person Scale - Revised
description: 18-item revised measure of sensory processing sensitivity across six subscales: Overstimulation, Sensitivity to Positive Experiences, Social Sensitivity, Depth of Processing, Emotional Reactivity, and Sensitivity to Details. Items use a 7-point scale (1=Not at all to 7=Extremely). An average score greater than 5 indicates a tendency towards high sensitivity.
citation: Pluess, M., Aron, E., Kähkönen, J. E., Lionetti, F., Huang, Y., Tillmann, T., Greven, C., & Aron, A. (2024). Evolution of the Concept of Sensitivity and its Measurement: The Highly Sensitive Person Scale-Revised. PsyArXiv. https://osf.io/preprints/psyarxiv/w7bqu. Note: This is a preprint; check https://sensitivityresearch.com/ or https://hsperson.com/ for the published article citation after mid-2025.
license: © Pluess et al. 2024. Permission granted to reproduce for personal, clinical, educational, and research purposes with citation. Unauthorized modifications prohibited. Contact m.pluess@surrey.ac.uk for other uses.

name: Luxembourg Workplace Mobbing Scale (LWMS)
description: Very brief (5-item) unidimensional instrument assessing workplace mobbing exposure in the general working population. Respondents rate how often difficult situations (criticism, being ignored, meaningless tasks, ridicule, conflict) arise with colleagues or a superior on a 5-point frequency scale. All items positively keyed; higher scores reflect greater workplace mobbing exposure. Validated in German, French, and Luxembourgish.
citation: Sischka, P. E., Schmidt, A. F., & Steffgen, G. (2021). Luxembourg Workplace Mobbing Scale (LWMS). Zusammenstellung sozialwissenschaftlicher Items und Skalen (ZIS). https://doi.org/10.6102/zis298

name: Multidimensional Scale of Perceived Social Support
description: 12-item self-report measure of perceived social support from three sources: Significant Other (items 1,2,5,10), Family (items 3,4,8,11), and Friends (items 6,7,9,12). Uses a 7-point Likert scale (1=Very Strongly Disagree to 7=Very Strongly Agree). Scoring is the mean per subscale and mean of all 12 items for the total scale. Widely validated across cultures and languages.
citation: Zimet, G. D., Dahlem, N. W., Zimet, S. G., & Farley, G. K. (1988). The Multidimensional Scale of Perceived Social Support. Journal of Personality Assessment, 52(1), 30–41.
license: Free for research and professional use with attribution; not open-licensed

name: Organizational Commitment Scale (ISSP)
description: 3-item measure of organizational commitment (OC) used in the work-orientations module of the International Social Survey Programme (ISSP). Items assess willingness to exert effort for one's firm/organization, pride in the organization, and willingness to forgo a better-paid job to stay. All items positively keyed. 5-point agree-disagree Likert scale; the recommended score is the unweighted mean of the three items after inverting them so higher scores indicate higher organizational commitment.
citation: Urban, J., Groskurth, K., & Schmidt, I. (2023). Organizational Commitment Scale (ISSP). Zusammenstellung sozialwissenschaftlicher Items und Skalen (ZIS). https://doi.org/10.6102/zis312

name: Partisan Identity Scale (PIS)
description: 8-item English-language scale measuring partisan identity strength: the degree to which a voter identifies with a political party. Adapted from the Identification with a Psychological Group (IDPG) scale (Mael & Tetrick, 1992), it captures a subjective sense of group belonging, the affective importance of party membership, and the affective consequences of lowered group status. The party the respondent identifies with is inserted into each item. All items are positively keyed (no reverse items). A 4-item short form (items 3, 6, 7, 8) is available. The scale targets partisans only and is not meaningful for respondents with no party attachment.
citation: Bankert, A. & Huddy, L. (2019). Partisan Identity Scale (PIS). Zusammenstellung sozialwissenschaftlicher Items und Skalen (ZIS). https://doi.org/10.6102/zis270

name: Personality Inventory for DSM-5 Brief Form
description: 25-item brief self-report measure of the DSM-5 maladaptive personality trait model, covering five broad domains: Negative Affect, Detachment, Antagonism, Disinhibition, and Psychoticism. Each domain is assessed with 5 items scored 0–3.
citation: Krueger, R. F., Derringer, J., Markon, K. E., Watson, D., & Skodol, A. E. (2012). Initial construction of a maladaptive personality trait model and inventory for DSM-5. Psychological Medicine, 42(9), 1879–1890. https://doi.org/10.1017/S0033291711002674

name: Quadrangular Love Scale
description: 40-item self-report measure of love across four dimensions: Compassion (items 1–10), Affection (items 11–20), Closeness (items 21–30), and Commitment (items 31–40). Each subscale contains 10 items rated on a 7-point Likert scale. Compassion and Affection reflect feelings toward the partner; Closeness and Commitment reflect feelings about the relationship. Validated in US and UK samples with high internal consistency (α = .86–.93 per subscale). Items are presented in random order; researcher-only facet labels are not shown to participants.
citation: Karandashev, V., & Evans, N. D. (2019). Quadrangular love theory and scale: Validation and psychometric investigation. Journal of Methods and Measurement in the Social Sciences, 10(1), 1–35. https://doi.org/10.2458/v10i1.23520

name: Risk Proneness Short Scale (R-1)
description: Single-item ultra-short scale measuring the psychological disposition of risk proneness (general willingness to take risks). The respondent rates how willing they are in general to take risks on a 7-point rating scale with labeled endpoints (1-7). The scale score equals the respondent's answer to the one item. English-language adaptation (validated in the United Kingdom) of the German source instrument by Beierlein, Kovaleva, Kemper, et al. (2015).
citation: Nießen, D., Groskurth, K., Rammstedt, B., & Lechner, C. M. (2022). Risk Proneness Short Scale (R-1). Zusammenstellung sozialwissenschaftlicher Items und Skalen (ZIS). https://doi.org/10.6102/zis286

name: Scale of Positive and Negative Experience
description: 12-item scale measuring positive (SPANE-P) and negative (SPANE-N) affect over the past four weeks, yielding an affect balance score (SPANE-B).
citation: Diener, E., Wirtz, D., Tov, W., Kim-Prieto, C., Choi, D., Oishi, S., & Biswas-Diener, R. (2010). New well-being measures: Short scales to assess flourishing and positive and negative feelings. Social Indicators Research, 97(2), 143–156. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11205-009-9493-y

name: WHO-5 Well-Being Index
description: 5-item measure of subjective well-being over the past 2 weeks. Raw score 0-25; percentage score (0-100) = raw score x 4. Scores of 50 or below suggest low mood warranting further assessment.
citation: Topp, C. W., Ostergaard, S. D., Sondergaard, S., & Bech, P. (2015). The WHO-5 Well-Being Index: A systematic review of the literature. Psychotherapy and Psychosomatics, 84(3), 167-176. https://doi.org/10.1159/000376585
